problems: ming-dynasty used 26 pages against a budget of 9 (a Ming conquest, Great Wall, Tibet, Hami, Nurgan, Luchuan and Qing-conquest pages were needed for the shape changes); four were thin. southern-ming used 8 against 5, and the Jurchen dossiers 6 and 4 against 2-5.

qing-dynasty (ea-08) should name wu-sangui-s-zhou, not southern-ming, as the counterpart of its 1673-1681 gains and losses, and li-zicheng and xi-dynasty for 1644; later-jin-dynasty should add jianzhou-jurchens and haixi-jurchens as predecessors.

Cliopatria 'Southern Ming' conflates three states: the Southern Ming (1644-1662), Tungning's Taiwan (1662 shape) and Wu Sangui's Zhou (1673 and 1677 shapes); verdicts wrong in southern-ming, years belong to kingdom-of-tungning and wu-sangui-s-zhou.
Cliopatria 'Li Zicheng' shapes of 1632 and 1636 cover Ming land (wrong); the 'Ming Dynasty' row starts 1375, not 1368.

Several ledger regions are stand-ins where no page gives a boundary (Jurchen discs, Xi and Zhou provinces); the Wu page and the Revolt page disagree on Hubei and the 11 provinces of 1676, so four provinces are drawn as contested.
ming-dynasty carries 8 resolve warnings, all for the place name Ruili, which the gazetteer lacks.
